Job Summary

The CU Student Government Program Coordinator plays a crucial role in supporting CU Student Government (CUSG) across its various branches, including the Executive Branch, Legislative Branch, Judicial Branch, Election Commission, Joint Boards, and Finance Board. This position is responsible for supporting CU Student Government in various administrative functions, including student leader support, hiring, onboarding and managing student employees and leaders, fiscal review and planning, procurement and CUSG board relations.

CU is an Equal Opportunity Employer and complies with all applicable federal, state, and local laws governing nondiscrimination in employment. We are committed to creating a workplace where all individuals are treated with respect and dignity, and we encourage individuals from all backgrounds to apply, including protected veterans and individuals with disabilities.

Who We Are

The Division of Student Life consists of 36 departments that provide student support and services dedicated to helping students become successful, curious, competent individuals during their time at CU Boulder.

CU Student Government (CUSG)

The University of Colorado Student Government (CUSG) is the official governing body of the over 38,000 students at CU Boulder. As the most autonomous student government in the nation, CUSG is responsible for allocating $37 million in student fees to improve the lives of all CU Boulder students. CUSG seeks to make a meaningful impact on the lives of CU Boulder students through advocacy, representation, allocation and legislation.

Responsibilities

What Your Key Responsibilities Will Be

Student Leader Support

Post and track student job and leadership opportunity announcements using Handshake and other CU specified avenues.
Receive, organize, and forward incoming applications to the appropriate hiring committee.
Inform and provide resources to each member of a hiring committee of CU Boulder’s policy on hiring student employees and best practices while conducting an interview.
Develop and implement position-specific hiring timelines for all CUSG’s positions and student leader positions to ensure compliance with university policy.
Assist in the design and facilitation of training and development for CUSG positions, student staff, and student leader positions.
Schedule interviews with CUSG branch leaders and appropriate stakeholders.
Coordinate the submission and approval of student employee timesheets, handling hiring and onboarding processes, exit procedures, and leave reconciliation.
Supervise and manage departmental student employees.

Administrative Support

Serve as the CUSG liaison with Student Life Employee Experience Liaison, to ensure payroll is processed for part-time salaried and student employees.
Work directly with Student Life Employee Experience to hire all student employees and leaders for CUSG, ensuring accurate pay amounts and term dates.
Assist employees with timekeeping submissions, ensuring accurate and timely processing of bi-weekly and monthly payroll.
Review and monitor CUSG’s student budget with a focus on ensuring staff stays within approved hours and aligns with CU Boulder policy.
In collaboration with Student Life Employee Experience, troubleshoot payroll issues related to hiring, onboarding, and exit procedures.
Coordinate onboarding instructions and support for new student staff hires around payroll information, hiring packets, work-study, supervisory change forms, and separating student staff leaving their position.
Coordinate with Student Life Employee Experience on payroll-related inquiries, hiring transactions, and payment discrepancies.
Manage users and permissions within relevant software, managing accounts and permissions as necessary.
Assist other users in troubleshooting issues related to software used by CUSG..
Coordinate with Office of Financial Aid to understand and address any issues related to the impacts of stipend-based compensation on student leaders.

Fiscal Management

Conduct high-level fiscal planning and reporting in partnership with the Finance Director, Finance Board Chair, CUSG Advisor, CUSG Office Manager, and Student Life Business & Finance, and CUSG.
Process purchase orders, standing purchase orders, and procurement for expenditure requests, ensuring compliance with university policies.
Place orders for office supplies, catering, event-related materials, and other operational needs.
Handle travel arrangements, reservations, and accommodations for CUSG members.
Ensure compliance with the Student Fee Regulations and all university policies.
Ensure all expenditures are appropriately authorized, documented, and reconciled.
Maintain organized financial records and expenditure files.

jobs.description:
🏛️ About GovWell

We the people — and the taxpayers — deserve good government. Yet today, interacting with government services is often frustrating and inefficient. GovWell is building the AI operating system transforming how governments serve communities, starting with local agencies.

GovWell replaces legacy software for municipalities and counties, empowering public servants to radically streamline public services and cut internal processing time for permits and licenses by up to 95%.

Founded in 2023, GovWell powers 5,000+ mission-critical processes for agencies in 35+ states serving millions of residents. The company has raised $35M in funding from Insight Partners, Work-Bench, and Bienville Capital, and the team works in person at GovWell HQ in New York City. Read more about our founding story in TechCrunch.

☀️ Why GovWell?

A mission that matters: Building AI-powered products to fix outdated government systems isn’t just a technical challenge—it’s a historic opportunity to improve our foundational relationship with government and ensure trillions of tax dollars result in high quality services. WATCH: Mission & Vision with CEO & Co-Founder Troy LeCaire
Real-world impact: GovWell’s product is the system of record for government services that affect millions of Americans. From streamlining permitting for small businesses to accelerating affordable housing development, your work will make an immediate difference.
Join a startup in hyper-growth: We’ve found product-market fit and are scaling the business very quickly (4X ARR growth in the last year). As an early team member, you’ll learn what it takes to build a successful startup. You’ll work closely with the founders while enjoying exceptional autonomy and ownership over your work.

🌟 Role Overview

When a city switches to GovWell, one thing has to go right before anything else can: their data. A decade of permits, parcels, inspections, and license records — often living in a 2009 Access database, a folder of CSVs, or a legacy system with no documentation — has to land in GovWell accurately. If it doesn't, our relationship with a new client is off to a bumpy start.

As a Data Solutions Engineer, you own that moment. You'll take whatever a city hands you — messy exports, inconsistent codes, half-mapped schemas, geospatial data of questionable quality — and turn it into clean, trusted production data. That means writing SQL/Python that finds the edge cases before they find you, leading calls with non-technical government staff, and making judgment calls on messy data that you'd stake the launch on.

You'll report directly to Ben Cohen (Co-Founder & CTO) and work across Deployment, Product, and Engineering — with real influence over how GovWell's onboarding process matures as we scale.

We have a hybrid work culture that combines regular in-person collaboration at our New York City office (3+ days per week) with flexibility to work remotely.

💻 What you’ll do

Own data migrations end-to-end. Work directly with government staff to understand their source systems, configure schema mappings and ingestion settings, run validations and dry-runs, and ensure accurate, complete data lands in GovWell.
Be the gatekeeper for data quality. Identify gaps, inconsistencies, and edge cases in legacy data before they become production problems. Make documented judgment calls within defined constraints — and prevent bad or unsafe data from ever reaching production.
Be the technical face of onboarding. Lead customer calls, clearly explain data requirements and tradeoffs, and guide agency staff through the transition from legacy systems to GovWell with calm confidence.
Make the process better as you run it. Use internal tools, templates, and playbooks to reduce time-to-launch and minimize manual work. Help build toward a future where migrations are predictable, repeatable, and fast.
Close the feedback loop with Product and Engineering. Document recurring issues, unmet assumptions, and tooling gaps encountered during migrations — helping the platform evolve based on what you see in the field.

🧠 Who you are

Required

2-4 years of hands-on experience in data migrations, ETL/ELT, technical implementations, or a closely related role working with messy, real-world production data.
Demonstrated ability to work directly in a Python codebase day-to-day (reading, debugging, and shipping changes via PRs) — ideally in a data/pipeline repo (e.g., Airflow DAGs, ingestion jobs, migration utilities).
Strong SQL proficiency used in practice for analysis, validation, reconciliation, and transformation work.
Experience translating ambiguous stakeholder requirements into concrete, testable migration/implementation plans (what we’re importing, what we’re not, and why).
Track record of operating in execution-heavy environments with high ownership and high attention to correctness (where mistakes create customer-facing trust issues).

Preferred

Experience with workflow orchestration and pipeline operations (Airflow, Dagster, Prefect, etc.), including interpreting logs, safe reruns, and handling large backfills/imports.
Experience with customer-facing implementation/onboarding work (especially where you need to explain constraints and tradeoffs to non-technical stakeholders).
Familiarity with geospatial data concepts or GIS tooling (e.g., ArcGIS, address/parcel data), or strong willingness to learn quickly.
Experience in B2B SaaS (or similarly complex product domains) where data correctness materially impacts user workflows.
Experience partnering closely with product/engineering teams to turn recurring operational pain into playbooks, tooling improvements, and system-level fixes.

🖥️ Our tech stack

SQL – your core tool for validation, reconciliation, and troubleshooting
Python – used in data workflows and automation
Airflow – for managing data migration pipelines
PostgreSQL – our core database
RedwoodJS, GraphQL, TypeScript, AWS – the broader software engineering environment you’ll interact with

💸 Compensation And Benefits

Competitive base salary.
Equity / stock options.
Medical, dental, and vision insurance.
401(k) program.

Compensation Range: $130K - $180K

Good interpersonal skills.

🏛️ About GovWell

We the people — and the taxpayers — deserve good government. Yet today, interacting with government services is often frustrating and inefficient. GovWell is building the AI operating system transforming how governments serve communities, starting with local agencies.

GovWell replaces legacy software for municipalities and counties, empowering public servants to radically streamline public services and cut internal processing time for permits and licenses by up to 95%.

Founded in 2023, GovWell powers 5,000+ mission-critical processes for agencies in 35+ states serving millions of residents. The company has raised $35M in funding from Insight Partners, Work-Bench, and Bienville Capital, and the team works in person at GovWell HQ in New York City. Read more about our founding story in TechCrunch.

☀️ Why GovWell?

A mission that matters: Building AI-powered products to fix outdated government systems isn’t just a technical challenge—it’s a historic opportunity to improve our foundational relationship with government and ensure trillions of tax dollars result in high quality services. WATCH: Mission & Vision with CEO & Co-Founder Troy LeCaire
Real-world impact: GovWell’s product is the system of record for government services that affect millions of Americans. From streamlining permitting for small businesses to accelerating affordable housing development, your work will make an immediate difference.
Join a startup in hyper-growth: We’ve found product-market fit and are scaling the business very quickly (4X ARR growth in the last year). As an early team member, you’ll learn what it takes to build a successful startup. You’ll work closely with the founders while enjoying exceptional autonomy and ownership over your work.

🌟 Role Overview

When a city switches to GovWell, one thing has to go right before anything else can: their data. A decade of permits, parcels, inspections, and license records — often living in a 2009 Access database, a folder of CSVs, or a legacy system with no documentation — has to land in GovWell accurately. If it doesn't, our relationship with a new client is off to a bumpy start.

As a Data Solutions Engineer, you own that moment. You'll take whatever a city hands you — messy exports, inconsistent codes, half-mapped schemas, geospatial data of questionable quality — and turn it into clean, trusted production data. That means writing SQL/Python that finds the edge cases before they find you, leading calls with non-technical government staff, and making judgment calls on messy data that you'd stake the launch on.

You'll report directly to Ben Cohen (Co-Founder & CTO) and work across Deployment, Product, and Engineering — with real influence over how GovWell's onboarding process matures as we scale.

We have a hybrid work culture that combines regular in-person collaboration at our New York City office (3+ days per week) with flexibility to work remotely.

💻 What you’ll do

Own data migrations end-to-end. Work directly with government staff to understand their source systems, configure schema mappings and ingestion settings, run validations and dry-runs, and ensure accurate, complete data lands in GovWell.
Be the gatekeeper for data quality. Identify gaps, inconsistencies, and edge cases in legacy data before they become production problems. Make documented judgment calls within defined constraints — and prevent bad or unsafe data from ever reaching production.
Be the technical face of onboarding. Lead customer calls, clearly explain data requirements and tradeoffs, and guide agency staff through the transition from legacy systems to GovWell with calm confidence.
Make the process better as you run it. Use internal tools, templates, and playbooks to reduce time-to-launch and minimize manual work. Help build toward a future where migrations are predictable, repeatable, and fast.
Close the feedback loop with Product and Engineering. Document recurring issues, unmet assumptions, and tooling gaps encountered during migrations — helping the platform evolve based on what you see in the field.

🧠 Who you are

Required

2-4 years of hands-on experience in data migrations, ETL/ELT, technical implementations, or a closely related role working with messy, real-world production data.
Demonstrated ability to work directly in a Python codebase day-to-day (reading, debugging, and shipping changes via PRs) — ideally in a data/pipeline repo (e.g., Airflow DAGs, ingestion jobs, migration utilities).
Strong SQL proficiency used in practice for analysis, validation, reconciliation, and transformation work.
Experience translating ambiguous stakeholder requirements into concrete, testable migration/implementation plans (what we’re importing, what we’re not, and why).
Track record of operating in execution-heavy environments with high ownership and high attention to correctness (where mistakes create customer-facing trust issues).

Preferred

Experience with workflow orchestration and pipeline operations (Airflow, Dagster, Prefect, etc.), including interpreting logs, safe reruns, and handling large backfills/imports.
Experience with customer-facing implementation/onboarding work (especially where you need to explain constraints and tradeoffs to non-technical stakeholders).
Familiarity with geospatial data concepts or GIS tooling (e.g., ArcGIS, address/parcel data), or strong willingness to learn quickly.
Experience in B2B SaaS (or similarly complex product domains) where data correctness materially impacts user workflows.
Experience partnering closely with product/engineering teams to turn recurring operational pain into playbooks, tooling improvements, and system-level fixes.

🖥️ Our tech stack

SQL – your core tool for validation, reconciliation, and troubleshooting
Python – used in data workflows and automation
Airflow – for managing data migration pipelines
PostgreSQL – our core database
RedwoodJS, GraphQL, TypeScript, AWS – the broader software engineering environment you’ll interact with

401(k) program.

Description

The CSP-HI Case Management Project Coordinator
is a dual-impact role combining expert case management with program coordination and administrative leadership. The CSP-HI funding stream through MassHealth supports housing stabilization and wraparound supportive services for individuals transitioning from chronic homelessness into permanent housing. As Victory Programs expands CSP-HI services across multiple programs, this role will play a critical part in developing and coordinating the agency’s CSP-HI operations.

The Coordinator is responsible for key program functions including outreach, referral management, client enrollment, compliance tracking, interdepartmental coordination, and support of ongoing program implementation. Collaboration is central to this role, as the Coordinator will work closely with multiple agency programs within Victory Programs to identify eligible clients, facilitate seamless service delivery, and ensure continuity of care.

In addition to program coordination responsibilities, this role maintains a dedicated caseload and provides comprehensive, client-centered case management to individuals navigating housing transitions, chronic health conditions, substance use, and mental health challenges. Services are delivered using a Housing First and Harm Reduction approach, supporting clients from housing placement through long-term tenancy stabilization.

Reporting to the Director of the Community Based Housing Division, the CSP-HI Case Management Project Coordinator
will help drive service quality, program development, compliance, and cross-program collaboration while supporting the continued growth of CSP-HI services throughout the agency.

Location:
434 Massachusetts Ave. Boston, MA (Hybrid Eligible after 90 days)

Essential Functions

Project Coordination

Coordinate day-to-day implementation of CSP-HI-funded program activities
Ensure compliance with all funding requirements, reporting deadlines, and documentation standards
Track program deliverables, outputs, and outcomes in alignment with funder expectations
Maintain organized systems for monitoring project milestones and required submissions
Serve as primary liaison regarding program operations
Support preparation of program reports, audits, site visits, and funder communications
Monitor data quality and ensure timely and accurate entry into required systems

Case Management Coordination

Provide coordination support to case management staff to ensure consistency in service delivery
Prioritize intraagency collaboration: work closely with VPI programs to ensure clients receive uninterrupted services when transitioning from temporary shelter or programs to permanent housing and ongoing stabilization supports through CSP-HI.
Assist in developing tools that support case managers
Support onboarding and training of case managers in program procedures and documentation
Provide ongoing training and coaching to staff, focusing on CSP-HI stabilization standards.
Monitor caseload assignments to ensure equitable distribution and timely service delivery.
Facilitate monthly internal agency team meetings and represent the program at state and partner CSP-HI meetings.

Direct Case Management & Housing Support

Maintain a direct caseload of clients at various stages of the housing continuum.
Assist clients with program enrollment, insurance navigation, and accessing primary/specialist healthcare.
Conduct strengths-based assessments to develop concrete, measurable, and time-limited service plans.
Support clients through the processes of lease-up, move-in, and housing stabilization.
Conduct regular home visits and community outreach to monitor housing stability, identify early warning signs of crisis, and provide immediate intervention.
Support clients with independent living skills, including budgeting, lease compliance, neighborhood engagement and household management.
Act as a liaison between internal/external housing providers, mental health services, and substance use treatment programs.

Non-Essential Functions

Represent the program in the community and to designated partners and funding entities.
Identify alternative funding sources supportive of the program mission.
Perform other duties as deemed necessary by your supervisor or their designee.

Essential Qualifications

Education/Experience (One of the following):
Bachelor’s degree in Social Work, Psychology, Public Health, or a related field.
OR Lived experience with homelessness, mental health, recovery, or chronic health management.
OR Minimum of 2 years of experience in human services (homelessness, mental health, or substance use).

Deep understanding of Housing First, Harm Reduction, and Trauma-Informed Care.
Experience managing multiple data systems.
Extensive experience building effective relationships and coordinating services across multiple programs.
Proven crisis intervention, de-escalation, and problem-solving abilities.
Reliable transportation for community-based outreach
Proficiency in MS Office and Google Workspace.
CPR Certification and TB Screening (both can be obtained upon hire).

Preferred Qualifications

Master’s degree in Social Work (MSW) or a related field.
Experience supervising staff and/or interns.
Certification in Peer Support, Recovery Coaching, or Community Health.
Fluency in Spanish or Haitian Creole.
A valid Massachusetts driver’s license with a safety driving points of 00, 99, 01, 02, or 03.
